 View Comments Wednesday will see light rain working into extreme Southern New England by the evening. Boston Globe New England is likely avoid major impacts from the second nor’easter in recent weeks, thanks to dominant high pressure protecting the area to our north, west, and east. 
 Tuesday looks to be partly to mostly sunny with temperatures rising to about 60 degrees — but we’ll feel the winds increasing throughout the day. 
 That said, there will be some effects from this storm, mainly the wind, as an offshore low-pressure area develops along a frontal boundary stalled over the North Atlantic and gradually strengthens over the next couple of days. 
 The good news here is that the storm track (jet stream) has been pushed over the open ocean — unlike the nor’easter a few weeks ago, when the jet stream sat directly over the eastern seaboard. 
 This means that we should see limited rainfall with this storm, with light to steady rain at times for portions of Southeastern Mass. and Southern Rhode Island from late Tuesday through Thursday. 
 Boston may actually stay dry for nearly the entire duration of this slow-moving storm. It will slowly drift to the northeast through the work week, but may be far enough offshore that rain doesn’t quite make it to the city. If anything, Boston may pick up a tenth to a quarter of an inch Wednesday and Thursday — not much to worry about. 
 The winds will be quite noticeable starting late Monday, with gusty conditions through Thursday — simply from the strong gradient between the high pressure and strengthening offshore storm. Gusty winds are like going down a slide — the high-pressure winds race down to the low-pressure areas, and the steeper the difference in pressure, the bigger the slope and faster the winds. 
 Winds will be strongest on the Cape and the islands, and from Boston to Providence, and areas in between will also experience strong winds. Gusts may reach as high as 40 to 45 mph by Tuesday afternoon and evening across Southeastern Mass. and the Cape and islands — and stay that way through most of Thursday. 
 Greater Boston to Worcester, and south of Providence, may see gusts reach as high as 25 mph through Thursday. 
 Surf will be quite high along the Southern New England coast from Tuesday through at least Thursday, with waves of 5 to 10 feet crashing along the shore — though there’s not too much of a coastal flood risk with this storm. 
 Temperatures will stay quite seasonable during this stretch, mainly because most of New England will see more sun than clouds during this stretch, thanks again to the blanket of high pressure. 
 It won’t be until Thursday night into Friday that temperatures really chill, setting up a frosty Friday morning with wind chills in the 20s for most. 
 High pressure will keep most of New England dry from Tuesday into most of Wednesday, but some showers do work on shore late Wednesday into Thursday. Boston Globe The jet stream is positioned farther east over the Atlantic, keeping the storm out to sea for the most part. Boston Globe Tuesday will see more sun than clouds across New England, while the storm meanders off the coast of Virginia. Boston Globe Wind gusts will increase throughout the day across Southeastern Mass. on Tuesday. Boston Globe Highs on Tuesday should reach the upper 50s to low 60s across New England. Boston Globe Wednesday will see light rain working into extreme Southern New England by the evening. Boston Globe Wind gusts will slowly increase throughout Wednesday. Boston Globe The nor'easter speeds up and passes nearby on Thursday. Boston Globe Thursday morning will continue to see strong wind gusts across Southeastern Mass. Boston Globe Flooding rain is highly unlikely, but 1 to 2 inches may fall across Southeastern Mass., the Cape, and islands by Friday evening. Boston Globe Friday morning will likely see wind chills in the 20s across most of New England. Boston Globe The forecast across Boston for the next seven days. Boston Globe There is a 40 percent chance that this storm may develop into a subtropical storm system as it drifts to the northeast. Boston Globe Tuesday breakdown
 Greater Boston: Mix of sun and clouds. Highs in the upper 50s, maybe touching 60. Turning breezy. 
 Central/Western Mass.: Mostly sunny with highs reaching the low to mid-60s. Breezy in the afternoon and evening. 
 Southeastern Mass.: Mix of sun and clouds, with more clouds in the afternoon. Highs in the upper 50s and low 60s. Winds increasing, turning gusty late. 
 Cape Cod and the Islands: Mix of sun and clouds, with more clouds in the afternoon. Highs in the upper 50s. Winds increasing throughout the day, gusty late. 
 Rhode Island: Partly to mostly sunny. Highs in the upper 50s and low 60s. Afternoon breeze. 
 New Hampshire: Mostly sunny with highs to the low 60s. 
 Vermont/Maine: Mostly sunny for both states, highs in the upper 50s and low 60s. 
 Connecticut: Mix of sun and clouds, highs in the mid-60s. Turning breezy.
